instruction: Browse Marvel action figures for kids and sort by lowest price.

metadata.explanation: Task requires browsing Marvel action figures in Kids category and sorting by price low-high (S=4). Maintains same complexity and evaluation structure as original task. No custom functions required.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator relies on highly site-specific CSS selectors (pmpSearch_breadcrumb, sbSelector, li.catAllProducts) that may not match the actual Kohl's website structure
The class_multiObject_li logic assumes a very specific HTML structure (li.catAllProducts > span) that may not exist on the target page
URL parameter check S=4 for sort order is fragile and site-version dependent
No validation that products are actually displayed or correctly sorted - only checks UI state elements (breadcrumbs and sort selector)
The evaluator doesn't verify actual product data, only navigation/UI elements, which means it cannot confirm products are actually Marvel action figures for kids
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add fallback selectors for breadcrumbs and sort elements using multiple selector patterns (aria-label, role attributes, etc.)
Verify actual product data: check that displayed products contain Marvel, action figures, and kids keywords in their titles/descriptions
Validate that product prices are in ascending order, not just that the sort UI shows Price Low-High
Add more robust URL pattern matching to check for multiple possible sort parameter formats (S=4, sort=price-asc, etc.)
Include postconfig to ensure page is fully loaded and filters are applied before verification runs
Consider extracting and comparing actual product prices from the first few results to confirm sort order
